name: Blackheath
description: An open heath southeast of London where the Kentish rebels mustered on 12 June 1381 before entering the city. Traditionally identified as the site of John Ball's sermon on social equality -- though, per this book's treatment of the sermon's sourcing, the surviving text is a later chronicler's reconstruction rather than a verbatim record taken at the scene.
story_hooks: The Kentish muster and John Ball's sermon, 12 June 1381
